content: The websocket reconnect loop was caused by the client treating HTTP 401 on the handshake as retryable; stopping retries on 401 fixes the loop.
Two different agents reproduced the same websocket loop only when the access token had expired but the refresh flow had not completed yet.
When debugging auth-related realtime failures, inspect the initial handshake status code before looking at channel subscription logic.
I suspected the socket server was dropping idle clients, but logs showed the disconnects happened before heartbeat setup, so that theory is probably noise.
A stale debugging note said reconnect backoff should ignore auth errors; current behavior needs the opposite because auth errors are terminal until credentials change.
The console spam from repeated reconnect attempts hid the original 401, so preserving the first failure reason makes future debugging much faster.
The websocket file imports five helpers.
